To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anisotropic bond strengths in the inter-atomic bonding of ferromagnetic metals can be used to explain the crystallographic structure of the metal, that the bond strengths can be calculated by density functional theory, and that the calculated bond strengths can be used to predict the structure of a material.

1) ferromagnetic ordering in Fe reduces the symmetry of its crystal structure from body-centred cubic to body-centred tetragonal, 2) the ground state crystal structure of δ-Pu is monoclinic rather than face-centre cubic and 3) the uniformity of nearest-neighbour bond strengths in a Pu–3% Ga alloy explains the stabilisation of δ-Pu in the alloy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of complex metals and alloys.
the electronic structure and bonding of complex metals and the way that this influences the way in which the atoms are arranged in the lattice.
the development and application of a new method to solve the crystal structures of metals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anisotropic nature of the electronic structure of the metal is the key to its behaviour.
anisotropic electronic structures should be included in crystallographic descriptions of materials.
anisotropic electronic structures are a key factor in the determination of the structure and properties of complex metals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electronic structure of a material is the most fundamental aspect to its behaviour and that the crystallography of the material should be determined by the electronic structure.
the crystallographic motif is a powerful tool for understanding and explaining complex materials.
the crystallographic motif of an anisotropic electronic or magnetic structure is a viable and useful concept in crystallographic analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crystal structure of metals is not necessarily cubic, but can be a distorted form of a cubic motif.
the anisotropic electronic bonding motif should be used to determine the crystallographic structure of materials.
anisotropic bonding is an important aspect of crystallographic determination that is often overlooked.
